requests.subject: Adding a rule/exception to required number of parent contacts
requests.details: For safeguarding, the schools need to enforce the collection of 2 parents (not just 2 contacts, 2 parents specifically) - most of their parents are able to comply. If a parent is unable to provide a second parental contact, they have an option to select why they cannot provide more details, and have to upload supporting evidence, and in completing this they can then proceed to complete the rest of the form with only 1 set of details provided.

requests.subject: Hard Stop Validation for Parental Responsibility
requests.details: Currently, the form allows a user to proceed and submit even if they have not designated at least one contact with Parental Responsibility. During testing, *Hampstead School* found a loophole where a user can add a contact, select "No" for PR, and still successfully submit the form. The system does not currently verify that at least one person in the contact list holds legal parental responsibility even if this question is required, if parent says no to all contacts, then theres no PR added.
requests.impact: Without this "Hard Stop," admissions officers have to manually email parents, ask for the information, and update the record themselves. This defeats the purpose of an automated digital form.
requests.solution: Implement a "Hard Stop" or validation rule identical to the existing Priority 1 Contact block. The form should prevent the user from moving to the next step or submitting the form unless the "Parental Responsibility" toggle is set to "Yes" for at least one contact.

requests.subject: Enable "Reset" functionality for Offers in "Offer Made" status.
requests.details: Currently, the "Reset" option (introduced to allow staff to amend Offer details) is only available once an Offer moves to the "Accepted" status. Staff users, frequently need to adjust Bill Payer Percentage settings or other offer-specific details after the offer is generated. It is common that parents change their minds or makes mistake after completing a step in the Offer phase.
requests.impact: This affects the workflow of school's admissions. The current workaround creates inaccurate audit trails (showing a parent accepted when they didn't) and adds unnecessary administrative steps. Allowing staff users reset during the "Offer Made" phase ensures parents have entered the correct details before the Offer Contract is generated and sent to them.
requests.solution: Update the visibility of the "Reset" button so that it is available whenever the Offer status is "Offer Made" or "Accepted". This would allow staff to jump back to the Bill Payer or other Offer steps without needing to change the student's status first.

*FEEDBACK ITEM #1*
*Feedback Subject:* Bulk deletion of uploaded documents (passports, attachments) by year/cohort
*Feedback Type:* Enhancement
*Feature Area:* Data Management / GDPR Compliance
*Details:* College needs ability to mass-delete uploaded documents (especially passport copies) for specific enrollment years to comply with data retention policies. Currently hundreds of student passport copies sit on system indefinitely with no admin-controlled bulk deletion option. This is particularly critical for students who applied but never enrolled - their sensitive documents remain stored.
Olga's team collects extensive documentation on application forms (passports, proof of address) for operational efficiency with small admin team. Once students enroll, most documents can be deleted (except for residency verification cases which are downloaded separately). The college needs to delete documents in bulk by year while retaining application form data fields (names, emails, tick boxes showing verification was completed).
*Importance:* Critical
*Impact:*
• GDPR/data protection compliance risk - hundreds of minor passport copies stored indefinitely
• Security risk if system is compromised - highly sensitive identity documents exposed
• No current way for admissions administrators to action their own data retention policies
• Creates operational burden requiring manual Applicaa support intervention
*Suggested Solution:*
1. Admin dashboard feature to select enrollment year (e.g., 2021-22)
2. Bulk select/delete specific document types (e.g., all passports, all attachments) OR all documents for that cohort
3. Generate deletion confirmation report showing what was deleted and when (for audit trail)
4. Option to delete entire application forms for non-enrolled students OR selectively delete specific question responses/attachments while retaining core application data

*FEEDBACK ITEM #2*
*Feedback Subject:* Document link security - URLs accessible without authentication
*Feedback Type:* Critical Security Issue
*Feature Area:* Document Storage / Security
*Details:* When admissions data is exported as CSV, it includes direct links to uploaded documents stored in cloud. These links can be opened in any browser WITHOUT requiring login/authentication. While the links aren't obvious (require knowledge of specific URL), if someone gains access to a CSV backup (e.g., through college system breach), they could access all student documents by copying links into browser.
Olga flagged this ~3 years ago but hasn't received confirmation whether it's been addressed.
*Importance:* Critical

• Compounds risk of data breach - not just names/addresses but identity documents
• Affects CSV exports stored in college backup systems

*Suggested Solution:*
1. Implement authentication requirement for all document access URLs (session-based or token-based)
